chapter: Leo Watson and the Panassie sessions
title: Kicking off tunes and keeping the hungover players straight
summary: The others depended on Bunn to start the tunes; he was tired of being called to keep things straight, and he cannot recall where "If You See Me Coming" came from.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, right. One thing I noticed, listening to the tape, is that you kicked off a lot of the tunes.
Some of them.
Well, quite a few. Like two bar and four bar introductions.
Yeah.
And I was wondering -- some people said a lot of the guys were hungover and you were the only one that was straight. That's what I heard from somewhere, you
Yeah, well that's true.
And so you would kick off with these intros and get everybody sort of -- together.
Yeah. They depended on me to start them off.
Uh-huh. Were you accustomed to that role? I mean, from the Spirits?
Yeah, unfortunately I was, yeah.
(Laughter)
The first thing they'd do is say, "Get Teddy Bunn, get Teddy Bunn, get Teddy Bunn. He'll keep it straight. He'll keep it straight."
Yeah. That gets old, doesn't it.
Yeah.
Having people keep those dudes straight.
Yeah. You get tired of hearing it.
(Laughter)
Some people ought to take care of themselves sometimes.
First thing you say, well, that's all they want me for is to kick off the thing.
(Laughter)
There's some real good solos there,
though.
Not for my talent, you know.
Well, of course, it all comes together.
Yeah.
At least I think so.
Musicians, yeah.
That song that you sang on --"When You See Me Coming".
"If You See Me Coming".
Yeah. Is that tune -- where did that tune come from? Is it just a traditional tune?
I can't remember that either.
Yeah.
Where it came from.
Because I've never heard anybody else sing it.
Evidently something come in my mind and I just sang it at the time they wanted me to do something like that.
It just popped into your head.
Yeah.
